17_marg1674: Which was the chief city of the Hevites, and fell to the lot of Benjamin, and was set apart for the Levites. It is strange, then, that Josephus says that Solomon came to Hebron to sacrifice on the brazen altar which Moses had made; unless perhaps he meant Hebron itself to be understood as the high place of Gabaon, because he first reigned there. For Gabaon is interpreted 'height' or 'hill of the kinsman'.
17_marg1675: Give me wisdom etc. He asks of God not gold, not riches, not earthly glory, but that he may know how to rule and judge the people of God. If the ruler of bodies chose this, much more ought the rulers of souls to choose it, that they may show the people of God the entrance to faith and the going out to hope.
17_marg1676: It signifies the ark, in which were the tables of the testament. For it is written above: "But the tabernacle of the Lord, which Moses made in the desert, and the altar of holocausts, were at that time in the high place of Gabaon" etc. But the ark of the Lord, after David brought it into his house, remained there until the temple was built.

17_marg1677: AND TWELVE THOUSAND etc. This number signifies the time of grace, in which the apostolic doctrine forms the people of the new Testament. And well are the chariots and horsemen of Solomon numbered by the number forty or twelve, because through both Testaments holy men, learned in the sacred letters, are fitted for God to sit upon, whom he, the supreme charioteer, guides at his nod.

17_marg1678: Because by the preaching of the two Testaments men are brought through the preachers to know the truth of faith, for the use of the true Solomon. Six hundred, then, that is, sixty tens, signify the perfection of the gospel teaching, in which the perfection of the law wholly consists; especially since our Redeemer, suffering on the sixth day, fulfilled all things that were written of him in the law and the prophets; whence he says: "It is consummated. And bowing his head, he gave up the ghost."
17_marg1679: [A hundred and fifty,] which are three fifties, and plainly signify the old Testament, because of Pentecost and the jubilee and the threefold division of Scripture; for it is said: "All things must needs be fulfilled which are written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me."
17_marg1680: AND SOLOMON DETERMINED etc. BEDE. The house which Solomon built in Jerusalem signifies the universal Church, because from the first elect to the last it is built daily through the grace of the true peacemaker; which is still partly a pilgrim in the world, partly, having escaped its toils, already reigns with him in heaven, where it is all to reign when the judgment is finished. To this house belong the angels, likeness to whom is promised us, the Lord saying: "For they are equal to the angels, and are the children of God" etc. To it belongs Christ himself, who says: "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. But he spoke of the temple of his body." Of us the Apostle says: "Know you not that you are the temple of God?" etc. If then he, by the humility he took on, was made the temple of God, and we by his Spirit dwelling in us, it is plain that that temple was a figure of all of us and of Christ himself: but of him as of the cornerstone, of us as of living stones built upon him. The tabernacle made in the desert designates the same house of God. But because that house [was made] on the journey by which they were coming to the land of promise, while this was built in the land of promise and in the city of Jerusalem; that, so that, carried from place to place by the Levites, it might at length be brought into the land of promise; this, so that, built at once in the homeland and the royal city, it might stand on an immovable foundation until it should fulfil the very reality of the heavenly figures: in that can be figured the labour and exile of the present Church, in this the future rest and blessedness. Or because that was made by the children of Israel alone, but this by proselytes and gentiles also, in that can be figured chiefly the fathers of the old Testament and the ancient people of God, in this the Church gathered from the gentiles; although the building of each house, taken in particular, shows by manifold figures both the daily labours of the Church and the future joys of the heavenly kingdom, and the election of the first Church from Israel and the salvation of all nations in Christ. And that Solomon is said to have determined to build a house to the name of the Lord and a palace for himself signifies the same thing, because the Church is both the house of God, which he inhabits for ever, and the palace of the heavenly king, in which he shows the greatness of his glory to all generations. The workmen of Solomon are all the elect who prepare themselves for the building of God by believing, working, and teaching others.
17_marg1681: Both by name and by his most peaceful reign he signifies him of whom Isaias says: "His empire shall be multiplied, and there shall be no end of peace." And Hiram, which is interpreted 'living on high', [signifies] the believers from the gentiles, glorious in life and faith, by whose work the Church is often helped and increased, and strengthened by imperial decrees against heretics, schismatics and pagans. Solomon, then, asks help of Hiram in the work of the temple, because Christ, wishing to build the Church, chose workmen not only from the Jews but also from the gentiles. Hiram sent to Solomon cedar and fir wood cut from Libanus, to be set in the house of the Lord; because the converted gentile world sent to the Lord men renowned in the world, but cast down and humbled from the mountain of pride by the axe of the Lord's rebuke, to be set at some time, in their measure, according to the rule of gospel truth. He sent also craftsmen to be set over the ruling of peoples, namely Dionysius the Areopagite, Cyprian, and many others. He sent also gold, that is, wise men, renowned also in genius. For all these, the gentile world, having given them, awaits from the Lord the gifts of heavenly grace: the wheat, that is, of the word of God, and the oil of charity, of the anointing and enlightening of the Holy Spirit.
17_interl2198: these things are told more fully in Kings
17_interl2199: the teachers from the gentiles, who cast down those glorious in the world from the haughtiness of pride and transfer them to the service of the true Solomon
17_marg1682: My apostles and first teachers, who form and instruct the teachers from the gentiles, lest they presume to teach anything wrong. For Solomon wanted Hiram's servants to cut wood for him because they were more skilled in cutting than his own servants; but he wanted his own servants also to be present, to show the cutters of what measure the wood ought to be made. For the apostles knew the words of the gospel more surely from the Lord himself; but the gentiles converted from errors to the truth of the gospel knew the errors of the gentiles more surely, and therefore overthrew them more subtly.

17_interl2201: he calls him his father because, having travelled abroad from the land of Israel, he taught him the fear of the Lord and the knowledge of the truth
17_marg1683: He shows that he was of the progeny of Salomith of the tribe of Dan, of whom we read in the book of Numbers. The Hebrews hand down that his father was a Hebrew of the stock of Ooliab of the tribe of Dan, who worked with Beseleel in the desert. And as to his calling him a Tyrian, the Hebrews say this was done by a transfer [of meaning]. For [unclear in the edition: "Zocri"] in their tongue is interpreted 'moulding'. For Tyre [so the edition: 'Chyros'], which they call Zor, sounds sometimes 'narrowness', sometimes 'moulding'.

17_marg1684: WHO KNEW HOW TO WORK IN GOLD, SILVER, BRASS, IRON etc. In all these the spiritual Hiram knows how to work, so that the adornment of the house of God may shine with worthy beauty before the eyes of men, and be made acceptable to God by the odour of good repute.
17_marg1685: AND WE WILL CUT etc. It signifies that the gentile world, having heard the fame of the gospel, sends divers persons through faith to baptism. Yet it belongs to the true peacemaker alone to unite them to the unity of the Church by absolving their sins through the sacraments of baptism; of whom it is said: "He upon whom thou shalt see the Spirit descending, and remaining upon him, he it is that baptizeth."
17_interl2212: who passed over from the gentiles into the fellowship of the people of God
17_marg1686: The workmen of the house of the Lord were of the children of Israel, of the proselytes, [and] of the gentiles: of the children of Israel, thirty thousand, who were sent to cut cedars from Libanus, as we read in Kings; of the proselytes, of whom namely he now speaks, the hewers of stones; of the gentiles, Hiram himself and his servants, who cut wood from Libanus with the servants of Solomon. All the races of men, then, by whom the Church was to be built went before in the building of Solomon's temple. For Jews, proselytes and gentiles converted to the truth of the gospel build the Church of Christ by living and teaching rightly.
17_marg1687: In Paralipomenon, instead of the three thousand three hundred overseers who are numbered in Kings, three thousand six hundred are written, for the perfection of lofty men. For in six [days] God completed the adornment of the world; and because holy Scripture teaches the faith of the Trinity and the works of justice, rightly are there said to have been three thousand six hundred.
